| Material | $\mu_{\text{mat}}$ | Relative Valuation Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wood` | `1.00` | Baseline organic structural timber. |
| `sandstone` | `1.25` | Sedimentary freestone; denser than `wood` ($1.00$), softer to quarry and dress than `stone` ($1.50$). |
| `clay` | `1.25` | Sun-baked/kiln-dried earthen material (referenced in `frame-adobe`); between `wood` ($1.00$) and vitrified `brick` ($2.00$). |
| `stone` | `1.50` | Standard fieldstone/ashlar masonry baseline. |
| `slate` | `1.75` | Fine-grained foliated metamorphic rock; cleaves into durable roofing/masonry slabs; above `stone` ($1.50$), below fired `brick` ($2.00$). |
| `brick` | `2.00` | Fired ceramic masonry unit. |
| `copper` | `2.00` | Base non-ferrous metal. |
| `cotton` | `2.50` | Woven textile substrate. |
| `granite` | `2.50` | Intrusive felsic stone of high compressive strength; between `stone` ($1.50$) and ornamental `marble` ($3.75$). |
| `iron` | `3.00` | Smelted ferrous metal; requires higher reduction temperatures than `copper` ($2.00$), below luxury `marble` ($3.75$). |
| `glass` | `3.00` | Kiln-fused silica panes requiring high-temperature vitrification and skilled casting; comparable to smelted `iron` ($3.00$). |
| `marble` | `3.75` | Metamorphic architectural stone. |
| `gold` | `10.00` | Precious metal upper bound. |
